From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: loch, lòch, lôch, łöch, and Łoch

English

[edit]
English Wikipedia has an article on:
Loch (surname)
Wikipedia

Etymology

[edit]

Two main origins:

  • Borrowed from German Loch, a topographic surname for someone who lived by a hollow or valley.
  • From Scottish Gaelic loch (“loch, lake”), a Scottish topographic surname.

Proper noun

[edit]

Loch (plural Lochs)

  1. A surname.
  2. A town in Bass Coast Shire and South Gippsland Shire, southern Victoria, Australia.

Statistics

[edit]
  • According to the 2010 United States Census, Loch is the 12496th most common surname in the United States, belonging to 2481 individuals. Loch is most common among White (88.35%) individuals.

Further reading

[edit]
  • Hanks, Patrick, editor (2003), “Loch”, in Dictionary of American Family Names, volume 2, New York: Oxford University Press, →ISBN, page 451.

German

[edit]

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /lɔx/, [lɔx], [lɔχ]
  • Audio (Austria):(file)
  • Audio (Germany (Berlin)):(file)

Etymology 1

[edit]

From Middle High German loch, from Old High German loh, from Proto-West Germanic *lok (“lock; hole”). Doublet of Lücke (“gap”) and Luke (“hatch”).

Noun

[edit]

Loch n (strong, genitive Loches or Lochs, plural Löcher, diminutive Löchlein n or Löchelchen n)

  1. hole; perforation
  2. hole in the ground; pit
  3. gap; bare spot
  4. (dentistry) cavity
  5. dungeon; underground prison
  6. (colloquial) prison; jail
  7. (colloquial) apartment, flat or house in a bad condition; dump
  8. (colloquial) boring small town or village
Declension
[edit]
Declension of Loch [neuter, strong]
singular plural
indef. def. noun def. noun
nominative ein das Loch die Löcher
genitive eines des Loches, Lochs der Löcher
dative einem dem Loch, Loche1 den Löchern
accusative ein das Loch die Löcher

1Now rare, see notes.

Synonyms
[edit]
  • (pit): Grube
  • (gap): Lücke
  • (dungeon): Kerker; Verlies
  • (prison): Gefängnis; Haftanstalt; Justizvollzugsanstalt; Bau; Kittchen; Knast
  • (boring town): Kaff

Etymology 2

[edit]

Borrowed from English loch, from Scottish Gaelic and Irish loch.

Noun

[edit]

Loch n (strong, genitive Lochs, plural Lochs)

  1. loch, lough (a lake or bay in Scotland or Ireland)
Declension
[edit]
Declension of Loch [neuter, strong]
singular plural
indef. def. noun def. noun
nominative ein das Loch die Lochs
genitive eines des Lochs der Lochs
dative einem dem Loch den Lochs
accusative ein das Loch die Lochs

Hunsrik

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Middle High German loch, from Old High German loh.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈlox/
  • Rhymes: -ox
  • Syllabification: Loch

Noun

[edit]

Loch n (plural Lecher, diminutive Lechelche)

  1. hole

Further reading

[edit]

Pennsylvania German

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From Middle High German loch, from Old High German loh. Compare German Loch.

Noun

[edit]

Loch n (plural Lecher)

  1. hole
  2. rent
  3. burrow
